expression: it should be possible to re-use existing artifacts to create further model elements instead of being forced to create every single modeling detail from scratch.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Support for re-usability of artifacts

expression: software-components shall not directly call the operating system or the communication hardware.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Software components independence from OS and hardware

expression:
Application software within AUTOSAR is organized in self-contained units called Atom
icSwComponentTypes. Such AtomicSwComponentTypes encapsulate the imple
mentation of their functionality and behavior and merely expose well-deﬁned connec
tion points, called PortPrototypes, to the outside world.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Definition of AtomicSwComponentType Encapsulation and Port Exposure

expression: AtomicSwComponentTypes (and also the more general SwComponentTypes may only interact by means of their PortPrototypes). Hidden communication dependencies that are not expressed by means of PortPrototypes are strictly forbidden.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: SwComponentTypes may only interact by means of their PortPrototypes

expression:
Please note that PortPrototypes actually need an additional model artifact, the PortInterface, for fully describing the details of the PortPro
totype. The concept of the PortInterface as another means for establishing a
high degree of re-usability is described in chapter 3.4.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: PortPrototypes need an additional model artifact, the PortInterface

expression:
As depicted in Figure 3.2, PortPrototypes can have the following semantics:
• A require-port (in technical terms: RPortPrototype) requires certain services or data.
• A provide-port (or PPortPrototype) on the other hand provides services or data.
• A provide-require-port (or PRPortPrototype) combines the ability to provide and require services or data in one entity.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Semantics of PortPrototypes

expression:
A PRPortPrototype is never considered unconnected, even if
there are no SwConnectors actually referring to it.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: A PRPortPrototype is never considered unconnected

expression: Two SwComponentPrototypes are eventually connected by hooking up a PPortPrototype or PRPortPrototype of one SwComponentPrototype to a compatible RPortPrototype or PRPortPrototype of the other SwComponentPrototypes. Please ﬁnd more information concerning the deﬁnition of “compatibility” in section 6.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Connecting two PortPrototypes

expression: PortPrototypes can be logically grouped into PortGroups. This mechanism is used for implementing mode management features and further explained in chapter 4.6.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: PortGroup

expression: As mentioned before, the term AtomicSwComponentType is a speciﬁc form of the general concept of the SwComponentType. The added value of an AtomicSwComponentType is that it can aggregate an InternalBehavior (see chapter 7).
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Added value of an AtomicSwComponentType

expression: The aggregation of SwcInternalBehavior is stereotyped (cid:28)atpSplitable(cid:29) to allow for adding the SwcInternalBehavior in a later process step. In other words, it is possible to completely develop the VFB view of a software-component and later add more details like InternalBehavior.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Adding the SwcInternalBehavior in a later process step

expression: The ApplicationSwComponentType is a specialization of AtomicSwComponentType for representing hardware-independent application software.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Definition of ApplicationSwComponentType

expression: The ParameterSwComponentType is a specialization of SwComponentType that can - in contrast to AtomicSwComponentType - not aggregate SwcInternalBehavior.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: ParameterSwComponentType cannot aggregate SwcInternalBehavior

expression: A ParameterSwComponentType shall never aggregate a SwcInternalBehavior and also owns exclusively PPortPrototypes of type ParameterInterface.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: ParameterSwComponentType

expression: a ParameterSwComponentType shall have the ability to aggregate InstantiationDataDefProps.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: ParameterSwComponentType ability to aggregate InstantiationDataDefProps

expression:
To mitigate this potential hazard it is possible to provide the AtomicSwComponentType along with an accompanying symbolic name that can be used for resolving the name clash. The symbolic name is provided by means of the attribute symbol of the meta-class Sym
bolProps owned by AtomicSwComponentType in the role symbolProps (for more information, please refer to Figure 3.6).
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Symbolic name of a software-component

expression: In particular, the RTE generator shall take over the value of the attribute symbol of the symbolProps owned by a given AtomicSwComponentType.If and only if symbolProps is not deﬁned the RTE generator shall take the shortName of the AtomicSwComponentType. For the generation of symbols for RunnableEntitys [TPS_SWCT_01001] shall be observed.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Usage of attribute symbol of the symbolProps

expression: If and only if the attribute symbol of a symbolProps owned by an AtomicSwComponentType exists, its value shall also be taken for preﬁxing the symbols generated for the RunnableEntitys owned by the AtomicSwComponentType.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Preﬁx symbols generated for the RunnableEntity

expression:
Of course, there is a residual risk that even in the presence of SymbolProps name clashes may occur. Therefore, the deﬁnition of naming conventions may facilitate the avoidance of name clashes to the further degree.
However, these naming conventions can (with the support of the meta-model, e.g. by utilizing SymbolProps or shortNamePattern) still only be deﬁned on the model level.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Naming conventions may support the effectiveness of SymbolProps

expression: The purpose of an AUTOSAR CompositionSwComponentType is to allow the encapsulation of speciﬁc functionality by aggregating existing software-components.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: CompositionSwComponentType

expression: Since a CompositionSwComponentType is also a SwComponentType, it again may be aggregated in further CompositionSwComponentTypes.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Nested deﬁnition of CompositionSwComponentTypes

expression: the deﬁnition of CompositionSwComponentTypes has no effect on how software-components interact with the Virtual Functional Bus (VFB). CompositionSwComponentTypes do not add any new functionality to what is already provided by the software-components they aggregate.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: CompositionSwComponentTypes effect on VFB and functionality

expression: As the main consequence, CompositionSwComponentTypes do not have any binary footprint in the ECU software.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: CompositionSwComponentTypes do not have any binary footprint

expression: In terms of the AUTOSAR meta-model, a composition of softwarecomponents realized by the meta-class CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes which in turn are typed by a SwComponentType.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes

expression: Therefore, a SwComponentPrototype implements the usage of a SwComponentType in a speciﬁc role.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: SwComponentPrototype implements a speciﬁc role

expression: In general, arbitrary numbers of SwComponentPrototypes that refer to speciﬁc SwComponentTypes can be created.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: arbitrary numbers of SwComponentPrototypes can be created

expression: Note that being a SwComponentType, a CompositionSwComponentType also exposes PortPrototypes to the out side world. However,the PortPrototypes are only delegated and do not play the same role as PortPrototypes attached to AtomicSwComponentTypes.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Delegation ports

expression:
Being a PortPro
totype attached to a CompositionSwComponentType has the following implications:
• The delegation has to follow the rules deﬁned in chapter 6.
• By creating PortPrototypes on the surface of a speciﬁc CompositionSwComponentType it is explicitly decided whether or not the contents of an “inner” port contained in the CompositionSwComponentType is exposed to the outside world.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Implications of being a delegation port

expression: a top-level composition might have (unconnected) PortPrototypes in order to allow for reuse as part of another system.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Top-level composition unconnected ports for reuse

expression: The recursive deﬁnition of a CompositionSwComponentType that eventually contains a SwComponentPrototype typed by the same CompositionSwComponentType shall not be feasible.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Recursive deﬁnition of CompositionSwComponentType

expression: Note that CompositionSwComponentType also aggregates the abstract meta-class SwConnector for connecting the SwComponentPrototypes contained among each other(see Figure 3.8).
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
Figure 3.8 Composition and the meta-classes aggregated
title: SwConnector

expression: AssemblySwConnectors interconnect PortPrototypes of SwComponentPrototypes that are part of the CompositionSwComponentType.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: AssemblySwConnector

expression: DelegationSwConnectors connect from “inner” PortPrototypes to delegated “outer” PortPrototypes.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: DelegationSwConnector

expression: A DelegationSwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of the same kind, i.e. PPortPrototype to PPortPrototype and RPortPrototype to RPortPrototype.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: DelegationSwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of the same kind

expression: In the case that an outer PortPrototype is referenced by multiple DelegationSwConnectors the semantic is the multiplication of the AssemblySwConnectors referencing the outer PortPrototypes.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Outer PortPrototype is referenced by multiple DelegationSwConnectors

expression: Each pair of PortPrototypes can only be connected by one and only one SwConnector.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: SwConnector between two speciﬁc PortPrototypes

expression:
[constr_1086] applies also in the case that two PRPortPrototypes are connected with each other. In particular, the roles
• AssemblySwConnector.requester
• AssemblySwConnector.provider
• PassThroughSwConnector.providedOuterPort
• PassThroughSwConnector.requiredOuterPort
do not establish a direction in this case.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Existence of SwConnector between two PRPortPrototypes

expression: An AssemblySwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of SwComponentPrototypes that are owned by the same CompositionSwComponentType
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: AssemblySwConnector inside CompositionSwComponentType

expression: A DelegationSwConnector can only connect a PortPrototype of a SwComponentPrototype that is owned by the same CompositionSwComponentType that also owns the connected delegationPortPrototype.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: DelegationSwConnector inside CompositionSwComponentType

expression: For the implementation of the attachment of a DelegationSwConnector to an inner PRPortPrototype the meta-class PPortInCompositionInstanceRef shall be used.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: PPortInCompositionInstanceRef shall be used for attaching DelegationSwConnector to an inner PRPortPrototype

expression: For any element in an unconnected RPortPrototype typed by a DataInterface there shall be a requiredComSpec that deﬁnes an initValue.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Unconnected RPortPrototype typed by a DataInterface

expression: PassThroughSwConnector can be taken to connect PortPrototypes owned by the same CompositionSwComponentType. In other words, PassThroughSwConnector creates a bypass inside a CompositionSwComponentType form the requiredOuterPort to the the providedOuterPort (or vice versa) without involving SwComponentPrototypes.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: The role of PassThroughSwConnector

expression: A PassThroughSwConnector is not allowed if the required outer PortPrototype is directly or indirectly connected to the provided outer PortPrototype without the placement of a SwComponentPrototype typed by an AtomicSwComponentType in the chain of SwConnectors.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Creation of a loop involving a PassThroughSwConnector is not allowed

expression: It is possible to specify instantiation speciﬁc properties of an RTEEvent by applying InstantiationRTEEventProps in the role instantiationRteEventProps.This allows to use the same ApplicationSwComponentType in different timing scenarios. Even if the scheduling is an issue of the SwcInternalBehavior, the instancespeciﬁc deﬁnition of timing needs to be speciﬁed on the level of a CompositionSwComponentType.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Instantiation-speciﬁc RTEEvents

expression: An InstantiationTimingEventProps shall only reference TimingEvent in the role refinedEvent. A reference to other kinds of RTEEvents is not supported.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: InstantiationTimingEventProps shall only reference TimingEvent

expression: A PortPrototype mainly contributes the functionality of being a connection point to the AUTOSAR concept.The details, i.e. with respect to what kind of information is actually transported between two PortPrototypes is deﬁned by the PortInterface.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: The role of PortPrototypes in the AUTOSAR architecture

expression: PortInterfaces (see Figure 3.14) are used to support a design-by-contract workﬂow, i.e. a PortInterface provides means to formally verify structural and dynamic compatibility between software-components.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: The role of PortInterfaces in the AUTOSAR architecture

expression:
Within the AUTOSAR concept, different ﬂavors of PortInterfaces are deﬁned:
• SenderReceiverInterface
• NvDataInterface
• ParameterInterface
• ModeSwitchInterface
• ClientServerInterface
• TriggerInterface
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Different ﬂavors of PortInterfaces

expression: Please note that the conceptual relationship of SenderReceiverInterface, NvDataInterface, and ParameterInterface is expressed by the deﬁnition of the abstract base class DataInterface.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: DataInterface is deﬁned as abstract base class

expression: From an abstract point of view, a PortInterface acts as a type for a PortPrototype. This means in particular that several PortPrototypes can be typed by the same PortInterface.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: PortInterface acts as a type for a PortPrototype

expression: It shall not be possible to connect PortPrototypes typed by PortInterfaces of different kinds. Subclasses of DataInterface make an exception from this rule and can be used for creating connections to each other.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Connect kinds of PortInterfaces

expression: A PPortPrototype typed by a ParameterInterface can only be owned by a ParameterSwComponentType.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Applicability of ParameterInterface

expression: In case of inconsistencies between the value of serviceKind and the actual implementation of the PortInterface the implementation of the PortInterface wins over the value of attribute PortInterface.serviceKind (which, for the intended purpose shall be considered an annotation rather than a semantically binding information).
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Inconsistencies regarding the value of serviceKind and the actual implementation of the PortInterface

expression: if the attribute serviceKind is not deﬁned in the context of a speciﬁc PortInterface the default value anyStandardized shall be assumed.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Default value if serviceKind is not deﬁned

expression: CompositionSwComponentTypes shall not own PortPrototypes typed by PortInterfaces where the attribute isService is set to true.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: PortInterfaces used in the context of CompositionSwComponentTypes cannot refer to AUTOSAR services

expression: SwcServiceDependencys can also be used for vendor-speciﬁc services.In this case the SwcServiceDependency shall not contain any of the standardized ServiceNeeds.
scope_path: 3 Overview: Software Components, Ports, and Interfaces
title: Usage of SwcServiceDependencys for vendor-speciﬁc services
